title: Kartoffels Torte (Potato Cake)
description: A cake made with egg yolks, potatoes, and citron.

ingredients.name: 8 Deka mashed potatoes with skin, strained

steps: Stir together 16 Deka finely ground sugar with 9 egg yolks

Add 8 Deka mashed potatoes with skin that have been strained, 4 Deka finely chopped citron, 1 teaspoon finely chopped orange zest, cinnamon, 1 crushed spice clove and 48 Deka roasted, strained potatoes
Stir for 1.5 minutes
Lightly fold in the whites of 9 eggs
Pour this mixture into a cake pan coated with butter and lined with white breadcrumbs
Bake at low heat for approximately 1 hour in the oven

title: Kastanien-Radetzky-Torte (Chestnut Radetzky Cake; Tourte à la Radetzky)
description: A cake made with egg yolks, chestnuts, and ground coffee.

ingredients.name: 32 decagrams roasted or cooked and sifted chestnuts
2 decagrams chopped pistachios and pignoli nuts

steps: Beat 24 decagrams butter until fluffy, then stir in 32 decagrams sugar and 16 egg yolks one after another.
Mix well with 32 decagrams roasted or cooked and sifted chestnuts and 1 knife-tip of grated coffee, then lightly fold in the beaten snow of 12 egg yolks.
Divide this mixture in two parts and fill into two buttered cake forms dusted with flour, baking at low heat for 1 1/2 to 3/4 hours.
Remove from the forms and place the baked plates on a sieve to cool completely.
Stir together 4 tablespoons sifted chestnuts, 8 decagrams sugar, 2 egg whites, and 2 tablespoons rum until well combined.
Spread this filling on one baked plate, cover with the second plate, and place on a baking sheet.
Beat 4 egg whites until stiff and fold in 16 decagrams finely sifted sugar, 2 decagrams peeled pistachios, and an equal amount of pignoli nuts.
Distribute this mixture evenly over the top of the cake, sprinkle with finely sifted sugar, and decorate with 2 decagrams chopped pistachios and pignoli nuts.
Dry in the open oven for 10 to 15 minutes, then remove and decorate the sides with meringue piping using a pastry bag, forming hollow ridges that should resemble cannon barrels.

steps: Work 21 deka butter with 5 deka flour by hand into a dough on a board
Roll flat with a rolling pin and let rest in a cool place
In a deep bowl, combine 14 deka flour and in its center pour 4 deka fresh yeast dissolved in 1/4 liter lukewarm milk

title: Krapfen feinfter Gattung (Fine Pastry Fritters)
description: A pastry dish made with yeast, melted butter, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: 60 Decaliter dried, warm, sifted, fine flour
1 liter milk, divided into 3 equal parts
7/8 Decaliter pork lard of better quality

steps: Heat a deep bowl and add 60 Decaliter dried, warm, sifted, fine flour and 4 Decaliter sugar with 5 grams salt.
Divide 1 liter of milk into 3 equal parts.
In one saucepan, add 1/8 liter lukewarm milk and dissolve 3 Decaliter fresh yeast in it.
In a second saucepan, add 1/8 liter lukewarm milk and stir in 14 Decaliter melted butter.
In a third saucepan, add 1/8 liter milk and sprinkle 10 egg yolks into it.
Make a well in the flour and gradually stir in the yeast dissolved in milk, then sift the milk with eggs through a sieve and add it, finally pour in the milk with butter.
Stir constantly while adding the liquids.

Beat the mixture into a light, fine dough by stirring everything well together, using a wooden spoon to work the dough mass from the sides, holding the spoon vertically against the bottom and pressing some dough with the back of the spoon against the hands, moving from right to left and from left to right.
Continue beating quickly and without interruption until the dough is fine, smooth, and shiny and releases from the spoon.
Place half the dough on a flour-dusted board, dust lightly with flour on top, and roll out very lightly with a rolling pin until the dough is about finger-thickness.
Mark the Krapfen with a cutter by pressing lightly without cutting through.
Place half a teaspoon of marmalade in the center of each marked circle.
Cut out round discs with a smaller cutter, place them marked-side up over the marmalade, and press down lightly with fingertips around the filling.
Using a slightly smaller cutter, cut out both parts together to form the fritter.
Place on a warm, flour-dusted board with the side that was previously on the board now facing up.
Cover finished fritters with a warm cloth.
Add remaining dough pieces back to the bowl and work in approximately 3 tablespoons of lukewarm milk, then proceed as before.
Place fritters three fingers apart on a board, cover with a warm cloth, and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size.
Heat 1 kilo beef lard and 7/8 kilo pork lard in a saucepan until very hot.
Place the first risen fritters in the hot lard with the lower side facing up, cover the saucepan, and after 2-4 minutes lift the lid.
When the lower side turns brown, turn the fritters with a wooden stick, leave the saucepan open, shake it slightly, and blow away the foam that forms so it does not stick to the fritters.
The fritters should be light enough to sink only halfway into the lard, which must be maintained at an even frying temperature.
Once both sides are baked, which takes 6-8 minutes total, remove with a slotted spoon and place on paper with the last-fried side down.
After a short time, transfer to another piece of paper.
Just before serving, dust lightly with vanilla sugar and serve warm and heaped on a napkin-lined dish.
Dissolved marmalade may be served separately in a sauceboat if desired.
This recipe yields approximately 40-50 fritters.

title: Krone von verschiedenen Zeigen (Croque en Bouche)
description: Prepared with chestnuts, chocolate, and whipped cream.
steps: Cut the sweet chestnuts crosswise and place them in a casserole with enough cold water to cover them

Remove the chestnuts with a spoon and pass them through a sieve into a deep bowl

Form walnut-sized balls from this mixture

Form somewhat smaller balls, dip them individually in hot praline sugar, and place them on the center of the two double rows

title: Lerchen in Krustaden (Larks in Croustades)
description: Prepared with larks, veal or liver, and lard.
steps: Take the number of larks according to the number of persons to be served, usually taking some extra pieces. After the larks are plucked and flamed, they are cut lengthwise along the entire back and the bones are carefully removed, though head and neck are left attached. Lay them all on a board that has been previously moistened with cold water and dust them with a little salt. Then place in each bird 1 teaspoon of veal or calves' liver pâté, sew the skin of the bird back together, filling the eye sockets with pâté and placing the beak in the breast. Put some lard in a casserole, place the birds with heads upward, closely packed together, and if necessary, fill any excess space in the casserole with bread pieces. Cover the larks again with lard strips, add 1/4 litre broth and some Madeira or white wine, and let them stew covered for 1/3 hour. Serve them in small croustades, placing one lark with head upward in each croustade instead of pâté, and lightly coat the larks with dissolved glaze. Strain the cooking liquid, skim off fat, mix with some demi-glace sauce, lemon juice and thinly sliced truffles, and serve alongside. Alternatively, the larks can be arranged upright in a butter pastry shell with pâté in the middle so that the heads point upward; serve with the mentioned sauce with some demi-glace. The larks can also be served with steamed rice, namely place the rice raised on a round, deep bowl, press with a spoon that has been dipped in hot broth in the middle of the rice, while pushing rice from the edge of the bowl toward the middle with a tablespoon so that the rice forms a nest shape, upon which place the larks in the middle. With each of these serving styles the larks are lightly coated with glaze and the mentioned sauce is served. They can also be served in a polenta nest.

description: Prepared with lard or butter or pork fat, breadcrumbs, and lamb.

steps: Place 8 deca of lard, butter, or pork fat in a casserole, add 1/2 teaspoon of chopped parsley, 1 pinch of marjoram (and if desired, 1/2 teaspoon of finely chopped onion), and roast.

For the strudel dough, place 1/2 liter of flour on a board, make a depression in the middle, add 1 pinch of salt, 1 whole egg, and add lukewarm water gradually, working it with the right hand or a broad knife into the flour while supporting with the back of a knife held in the left hand.

Knead it on the board until it separates from your hand.
Dust the board with flour, place the dough on it, work it with the palm and fingers until blisters appear on the dough.
Place the dough on a flour-dusted board so that the worked side is on the bottom and the smooth, pointed side is on top.
Cover it with a deep, warm bowl and let it rest for 1/3 hour.
Cover a table with a cloth, dust it well with flour, place the dough in the middle, dust it with flour, and stretch it somewhat with a rolling pin (Strudel roller).
Then stretch it out fully by holding both hands so that the thumbs point inward and the dough rests on both index fingers, stretching the dough over the cloth to a certain length.
Then lay it on the cloth and stretch it completely thin with your fingertips.
Cut away the edges, which never become completely thin, then brush the dough with beaten eggs using a brush and distribute the cold filling evenly along the edge of the dough.
Fold the dough over on one side 3 fingers wide, sprinkle this fold with the remaining filling, and roll up the dough together by holding the cloth lightly raised.

Dust the strudel lengthwise with flour, divide it with a wooden spoon dipped in water into pieces of desired size (approximately 2-3 fingers wide) so that when pressed up, the filling is pushed back on both sides of the piece and the dough closes.
Press it together on both sides with two fingers and the thumb and place it on a flour-dusted board.
Place the strudel pieces in simmering salted water and cook covered for 10-12 minutes.
Then remove them with a skimmer and place them in the hot soup, which should come to the table immediately covered.
Note that the lung strudel, like all cooked strudels that follow, must be served immediately after being removed from the simmering water, as they become firm with longer standing.

description: Prepared with beef, bacon, and pork or tongue.

steps: Remove the skin from the 2 kilos of beef, salt it, and lard it alternately with half-finger-long and pencil-thick pieces of bacon and salted pork rinds or salted tongue, then shape it nicely round.

Line a cassole with onion, root vegetables, 1 bay leaf, thyme, several sprigs of fresh parsley, bacon and ham, place the meat on top, pour some broth and ½ liter wine over it, cover with paper brushed with butter, seal with a fitting lid, and braise the meat slowly.

Remove the meat, strain the sauce and set it aside.
Finely chop the cooked ham or bacon that was in the pot and mix it with ½ kilo calf forcemeat (cold pâté forcemeat).
Prepare a pâté from butter dough as indicated for the Goose Liver Pâté, line it with thin bacon slices, and brush the bottom with 2 fingers high of the forcemeat prepared above.

Place the meat on top, brush it with the remaining forcemeat, cover this with thin bacon slices and cover them with a small-finger-thick dough plate, which is scored several times with a knife and then brushed with beaten eggs.
Bake the pâté for 1½ to 2 hours at moderate heat in the oven.
After this time, loosen and remove the lid, pour the strained sauce inside, put the lid back on, and set the pâté to cool.

description: A pastry dish made with egg yolks, yeast, and butter.

steps: Beat the butter until fluffy and mix well with the finely ground sugar and salt

title: Marmelade von Aprikosen (Apricot Marmalade)
description: A fruit preserve made with apricot, apricots, and sugar.
steps: Take 8 pounds of very ripe apricots
Remove the pits
Press through a fine sieve until nothing remains but the skins, which are discarded
Place the pressed apricots over low charcoal heat
Allow the liquid to evaporate
Shell and cut the apricot kernels lengthwise
Add a handful of these kernels to the marmalade
Stir well and set aside
Clarify and cook 5 pounds 8 loth of sugar as described
Carefully stir in the marmalade
When it begins to thicken and drops cleanly from a spoon, set it to cool
Fill into jars or boxes

title: Marmelade von Kirschen (Cherry Marmalade)
description: A fruit preserve made with cherries and sugar.
steps: Wash the cherries and remove the stems
Pit them with a pointed stick
Place in a casserole over a charcoal fire
Let the liquid cook down somewhat, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon until reduced to half
Clarify 6 pounds of sugar and cook until it reaches the small crack stage (petit casse), which is when a drop in cold water cracks between the teeth
Add the cherries to the sugar
Stir well over the charcoal fire until it reaches the proper consistency, which is when you can see the bottom of the casserole when stirring

title: Marzipan Ham (Marzipan-Schinken)
description: Prepared with dough, chocolate, and sugar.
steps: Take 8 pounds marzipan dough and work it with finely ground sugar
Divide the mass into two unequal parts of 5 and 3 pounds
Color the larger portion red and season it with 1 loth cinnamon and 1 loth cloves, both finely ground
Form the known ham shape
With a knife make cuts in the middle of the red dough, which represents the lean meat
Fill them with white dough, which represents the fat
Stretch the rest of the remaining white marzipan dough with a rolling pin and lay it as an upper fat layer, 2 to 3 fingers high, done skillfully and naturally
To represent the rind of the ham, cook quarter pound chocolate in water quite thick
Brush the surface of the ham several times with it
The chocolate must be applied warm
If you want to make this confection more delicious, take some vanilla or chocolate and sprinkle the rind with crumbled macaroons, as cooks cover cooked ham with a bread crust

title: Marzipan Raspberries (Himbeeren von Marzipan)
description: Prepared with dough, juice, and raspberry jelly.
steps: Take 1 pound marzipan dough, juice of 4 lemons, quarter pound raspberry jelly, and some cochineal
Stir everything well together with a wooden spatula
Since the mass becomes somewhat thin from the addition of these liquids, thicken it through addition of ground sugar and a handful of extracted flour
Form raspberry-like balls from this dough
Let them dry well on paper for 8 to 10 days
When this is done, pour a quarter seidel raspberry juice into a deep earthen vessel
Add some powdered sugar and some cochineal
Throw a handful of marzipan raspberries in and color them in it

Have ready a vessel with granulated sugar (a la gréle) - this is made by separating the very fine sugar dust from ground sugar through a silk sieve, then sieving what remains through a hair sieve, what stays in this is called in technical language granulated sugar
Roll the marzipan fruits moistened with raspberry juice in this granulated sugar so the grains adhere firmly to them
Lay them carefully to dry

description: Prepared with anchovies or mushrooms, fat, and potatoes.
steps: Trim the meat of skin, fat and bone, wipe it off, tap lightly with the back of the knife, salt, pepper it.

title: Matelote (Sailor's Stew) from Carp (Carp à la matelote)
description: Prepared with carp, eel, and onion.

ingredients.name: parsley and celery, all finely chopped
5 grains of each type of spice

steps: Scale, gut and clean 1 carp, then cut it and 1 small fresh eel into 2-finger wide pieces

In a casserole, place 8 decilitres butter with 1 large Spanish onion, 1 piece yellow turnip, parsley and celery, all finely chopped, 1 bay leaf, 4 sprigs thyme, 5 grains of each type of spice, 1 spice clove, and some nutmeg
Layer the carp and eel pieces and small pieces of calf's brain on top
Pour 1 litre red wine and 1/2 litre broth over
Mix 16 decilitres butter with 12 decilitres flour and place on top
Simmer covered for approximately 3/4 hour, then set aside for 1/4 hour
Arrange the fish pieces on a platter, garnish with small roasted onions, stewed mushrooms, crayfish cooked in wine, and toasted bread pieces
Pour the sauce, which must be thick and defatted, over the top

title: Matrosenfleisch (Sailor's Meat)
description: Prepared with chops, anchovies, and fat.
steps: Remove skin from meat
Cut first into strips, then into diagonal cubes
Season with salt and pepper
Heat 6 dkg fat in a casserole
Toast 1 large finely chopped onion
Add 1 small teaspoon paprika
Deglaze with a splash of cold water
Add the meat
Pour in some vinegar and water
Cover and braise for 2 hours, adding water occasionally
After 30 minutes, add the boned and finely chopped anchovies
Let braise together
Serve on a round or rectangular platter
